note: The entry follows Holmgren's 1910 original description (soldier and worker), published as Eutermes Sanctae-Anae. The original is a library OCR text of a BHL scan (Zenodo/Plazi mirror); the German original description was read line by line; figures that the OCR scrambled beyond confirmation are not listed.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head chestnut-brown; antennae and body sclerites rusty yellow; anterior part of the pronotum slightly brownish. Head with only a few bristles; abdominal tergites smooth with marginal bristles only. Head almost circular apart from the nasus; nasus of normal length and conical; frontal outline with an indistinct elevation at the base of the nasus, or none at all. Antennae 13-segmented: segment 3 one and a half times as long as segment 2; segment 4 only slightly longer than segment 2; segment 5 slightly longer than segment 4. Pronotum a shallow saddle, anterior margin distinctly concave. The body length, head length and head width are damaged by the OCR in the original printing (only 3 specimens measured), so they are not listed.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head plate and transverse band glossy brown; clypeus white-yellow; cephalic sutures, genae, antennae and mouthparts glossy rusty yellow to white-yellow. Head covered almost only with microscopic hairs, with a few longer bristles besides; abdominal tergites with very short fine hairs and with marginal bristles. Head broadly oval; cephalic sutures open and very distinct; fontanelle ill-defined and elongate; clypeus slightly shorter than half its width. Antennae 14-segmented: segment 3 longer than segment 2 but less than twice as long; segment 4 shorter than segment 2; segment 5 slightly longer than segment 4 but almost not as long as segment 2. Pronotum a rather deep saddle, anterior margin concave. Worker body length 5 mm, head length 1.81 mm, head width 1.08 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The original was published as Eutermes Sanctae-Anae n. sp., with the synonym Eutermes arenarius subsp. proximus var. a Silvestri. Type locality S. Ana, Misiones, Argentina (collected by Silvestri).
